subject: Bridgeline weekly — QBR prep & OKR check-ins
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Bridgeline weekly — QBR prep & OKR check-ins

Morning all — sharing a compact update for this week ahead of the QBR draft review (slides attached). I kept items to wins / risks / asks so execs can scan quickly.

Wins:
- Hosted API latency targets: p95 steady at 120ms for the week; new kernel selection rollout reduced tail latency on rtx-pools by ~18%.
- Customer traction: ACME POC completed end-to-end e2e test, ingestion pipeline confirmed for 2M events/day.
- Console: rollout of route-level cost breakdown is live for 50% of traffic; early feedback positive from 3 pilot teams.

Risks / Concerns:
- Dedicated capacity forecast: utilization for Q4 commit looks tight if ACME scales to 2.5M tokens/day; headroom only 12% under current autoscale profiles.
- Quantization regressions: a small uptick in hallucination rate on the 8-bit Llama variant on long-context prompts (observed on our regression harness).
- QBR slide alignment: some metrics (latency-by-model) are still pending final reconciliation from infra — delaying final deck by ~24–48h.

Asks / Decisions Needed:
1) Approve a temporary burst-capacity add for ACME pilot through end of quarter (+1 dedicated node pool) to smooth onboarding. If yes, I'll route to finance for a short-term committed bump.
2) Confirm priority on addressing quantization regression — RA/Research should get 2 sprint-weeks; if leadership prefers, we can instead pin ACME to the FP16 variant for their pilot.
3) Laura: can you confirm whether we should show pre- or post-reconciliation latency numbers in the QBR (I recommend pre with a reconciliation footnote).

Attachments: QBR_slide_v1.pdf (pdf, 2.3MB)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq9-example-drive-link

Thanks — I’ll update the deck after decisions.

—
Soojin Lee
VP, Platform & Ops
Redwood Inference
[attachment: QBR_slide_v1.pdf]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeline weekly — QBR prep & OKR check-ins

Thanks Soojin — concise and helpful. A couple quick points: 

- I support the temporary burst capacity for ACME to avoid onboarding friction. Please get a finance estimate (cost delta) and we can greenlight for 30 days.
- On quantization: I want a quick experiment plan before we allocate 2 sprint-weeks. Maya — can you run a 48-hour triage: reproduce on our regression harness (long-context set) and attempt the recommended fallback (pin to FP16) and report delta? Put results in the shared drive.
- For QBR: show pre-reconciliation numbers but add an appendix slide with reconciled numbers and a short note on reconciliation timing.

Also attaching the p95 / p99 export Markus requested this morning for the rtx pools.

Attachments: latency-metrics-2027-07.csv (csv, 120KB)

—
Markus
Chief Product Officer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: latency-metrics-2027-07.csv]

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeline weekly — QBR prep & OKR check-ins

Markus / Soojin — on it. Quick status and plan: 

- Reproduction: I can reproduce the hallucination/regression on the 8-bit variant on our long-context suite; failure rate ~3.9% vs baseline 1.1% on a 2k token workload.
- Short experiment (48h): will run two branches — A) FP16 pin for ACME pilot and B) targeted kernel tuning + small dequant fusion patches on the 8-bit path. I’ll log results to the drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq9-example-drive-link/quantization-triage
- Resource ask: need 2 dev-weeks from infra kernel team for the dequant work (estimate may drop after initial triage). If leadership prefers the conservative approach, we’ll pin ACME to FP16 by default.

Note on burst capacity: I’ll add a short note in the ACME action plan with the scaling profile we recommend if we add +1 node pool (includes expected cost delta).

On QBR deck: I did a quick pass on slide 4 (usage econ) and left inline notes. If anyone wants to review before I apply, ping me and I’ll share edit access.

—
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
